samples.summary: New `folderId` on the v1 document PATCH is accepted through an inline body type with no DTO, so neither `folderId` nor `title` gets any validation (the web equivalent validates both)
samples.evidence: `update()` binds `@Body() body: { title?: string; folderId?: string | null }`. Because the metatype is a plain object literal type, the global `ValidationPipe({whitelist:true, forbidNonWhitelisted:true})` in packages/backend/src/main.ts:66 is a no-op for this handler — as the change's own spec comment at documents.controller.spec.ts:259 states. The web route for the same operation uses `UpdateDocumentDto` (packages/backend/src/document/document.dto.ts:92-106) which enforces `@Length(1,200)` on `title` and `@IsUUID()` on `folderId`. On /api/v1 an attacker with a write-scoped key can therefore (a) write an unbounded `title` (only the JSON body limit applies) where the browser path caps at 200 chars, and (b) send a non-string `folderId` (e.g. `{"folderId":{"contains":"x"}}`) or a malformed uuid straight into `folderService.assertSameWorkspace` → `prisma.folder.findUnique({where:{id: <value>}})` (folder.service.ts:75), producing a PrismaClientValidationError/P2023 surfaced as a 500 rather than a 400. No SQL injection (Prisma parameterizes) and no privilege escalation was reachable — the mass-assignment that the old `data: body` allowed is genuinely closed — but the input-validation parity with the web DTO is missing. Searched: main.ts pipe config, document.dto.ts, folder.dto.ts, grep for `data: body`/`...body` across backend/src (no other mass-assignment remains).

samples.summary: Folder delete is gated on the *target* folder's author only, but the schema cascades descendants — so a plain member can destroy sub-folders authored by other members
samples.evidence: `remove()` checks `isManager(folder, req)` for the named folder only, then calls `folderService.delete(folderId)` (folder.service.ts:43). `Folder.parent` is `onDelete: Cascade` (prisma/schema.prisma:137), so every descendant folder is deleted regardless of its own `authorID`. `create()` (folders.controller.ts:88-105) lets any member create a folder under any parent in the workspace with no manager check on the parent, so member B's folder can legitimately sit under member A's, and A deleting theirs destroys B's. The documents themselves are `SetNull` (schema.prisma:123) so no document is lost. This is exact parity with the pre-existing web route (packages/backend/src/folder/folder.controller.ts:106-119), so the change does not introduce the semantics — but it newly exposes them to non-human API-key callers, and the controller comment at folders.controller.ts:153 characterizes the delete as 'non-destructive by schema' without noting the descendant-authorship gap.

samples.summary: `POST .../documents/:id/copy` duplicates blob bytes and is reachable by an automated credential with no per-route throttle, giving storage amplification
samples.evidence: `copy()` is gated on membership only and delegates to `DocumentCopyService.copy`, which for `pdf`/`image`/`file` documents performs a server-side `fileService.copy(source.fileId)` (document-copy.service.ts:198) — up to the 25 MB upload cap per call, with no quota. Unlike `ApiV1FilesController` (files.controller.ts:50-52) and the image controllers, `ApiV1DocumentsController` mounts no `@Throttle`, so only the global 120 req/60 s bucket applies: ~120 copies/minute of a large PDF per key. The web copy route has the same exposure, but it required a human session; this change makes it reachable by a long-lived, script-driven API key, which is what raises the abuse likelihood. Not traced to a concrete outage, hence low confidence.

samples.summary: `GET /folders` (like every other v1 read route) enforces no `read` scope, so a key minted with `scopes: ['write']` can enumerate the folder tree
samples.evidence: `ApiKeyWriteScopeGuard.canActivate` returns `true` immediately for any non-mutating method (api-key-write-scope.guard.ts:42) and nothing else reads `req.user.scopes`. `ApiKeyService.create` lets an owner mint an arbitrary scope array (api-key.service.ts:27), and its own doc comment calls `scopes` 'a real capability'. So a write-only key reads the new folder listing — and every other v1 GET. Pre-existing across the whole surface rather than introduced here; noted because the new route inherits it and the design docs in this change describe scopes as an enforced gate. Searched: grep for `scopes` across backend/src — the only consumer is the write-scope guard.
